description: The 17 announcement categories. weight (0-100) is the base priority, higher shows first. is_routine collapses the filing into the 'routine filings' row. default_alert is the out-of-the-box alert preference; the user can change it. card_type picks the card layout: results, management, one_liner or surface_only. Negativity bias: risks and red flags outrank good news. Weights are starting points; the priority scorer may adjust per filing (a credit downgrade, a large miss in results). why is the short line shown on a card to explain its rank.

categories.label: Litigation & regulatory action
categories.why: Legal or regulatory action can move a stock fast
categories.rationale: Court orders, regulator notices, penalties and tax demands can reprice a stock overnight; negativity bias puts them first.

categories.label: Promoter pledging
categories.why: Pledged promoter shares signal financial stress
categories.rationale: A new or invoked promoter pledge signals financial stress; a release is good news and should rank lower.

categories.label: Financial results
categories.why: Quarterly results are the most material filing
categories.rationale: The most material periodic filing; gets the full Revenue, EBITDA, PBT and PAT card with QoQ and YoY. A large miss should outrank a clean beat.

categories.label: Management change
categories.rationale: CEO, CFO, director and auditor changes move stocks, exits most of all; the card adds a short bio of the incoming person.

categories.label: M&A and restructuring
categories.rationale: Acquisitions, mergers, demergers and stake sales change what the company is; one line on what and how much.

categories.label: Credit rating
categories.why: Ratings affect what the company pays to borrow
categories.rationale: Downgrades and negative outlooks are red flags and should be escalated; plain reaffirmations should be demoted.

categories.label: Fund raise
categories.why: Raising money can dilute shareholders or add debt
categories.rationale: Equity raises dilute and big debt raises change leverage; one line on size and terms.

categories.label: Bonus & split
categories.why: Corporate action with a record date
categories.rationale: Rare corporate action with a hard record date; cheap to alert and easy to miss.

categories.label: Capex & expansion
categories.rationale: Forward-looking and often promotional; medium priority, no ping by default.

categories.label: Dividend
categories.rationale: Useful but usually expected; one line with the amount and record date, no ping by default.

categories.label: Press release
categories.rationale: Mostly marketing, occasionally an order win or a launch; one line for the so-what, no ping by default.

categories.label: Unclassified
categories.why: Could not be classified, so it is shown rather than hidden
categories.rationale: Anything the rules cannot place stays visible at low priority instead of being hidden as routine; ambiguous ones go to the cheap model.

categories.label: Insider trading
categories.rationale: Mostly routine trade disclosures, so collapsed; a very large promoter sale could be escalated later.

categories.label: AGM / EGM
categories.rationale: Meeting notices and outcomes are routine governance; collapsed.

categories.label: Earnings call
categories.rationale: Call schedules and recordings are routine; transcripts feed the Pull side and are not pushed.

categories.label: Postal ballot
categories.rationale: Voting notices and results are routine governance; collapsed.

categories.label: Investor meetings
categories.rationale: Analyst and investor meet intimations are noise; collapsed.
